FIN-003.purpose: Work out the monthly repayment and total cost of an amortising business loan, including an arrangement fee.
FIN-003.scope: Fixed-rate, capital-and-interest business loans repaid monthly. Variable rates, drawdown facilities, invoice finance and asset finance are out of scope.
assumptions: A fixed interest rate for the whole term.
Equal monthly payments with no payment holidays.
Interest accrues monthly on the reducing balance.
FIN-003.formula: Level payment from the standard annuity formula `P = (A x r) / (1 - (1+r)^-n)` where `A` is the amount financed, `r` the monthly rate and `n` the number of months. Where the fee is financed it is added to `A` and therefore attracts interest; where it is paid up front it is excluded from `A` but still counted in the total cost of credit.
FIN-003.boundary: An illustration only. It is not a quote, a credit decision, or an offer of finance, and lenders apply their own pricing and affordability rules.
FIN-003.methodology: Benchmarks were derived independently by bisection on the simulated closing balance and by month-by-month interest simulation, not by calling the production engine.

FIN-004.purpose: Work out the repayments on a loan secured against property, and the resulting combined loan-to-value.
FIN-004.scope: Fixed-rate second-charge and secured personal loans repaid monthly, plus a combined LTV against an existing mortgage.
assumptions: A fixed interest rate for the whole term.
The existing mortgage balance and property value are as at today.
Equal monthly payments.
FIN-004.formula: Same annuity formula as FIN-003. Combined LTV is `(existing mortgage + new loan) / property value`.
validation: Property value of zero suppresses the combined LTV rather than dividing by zero.
FIN-004.boundary: An illustration only, not a quote or credit decision. Because the loan would be secured on the borrower's home, the result carries an explicit repossession warning.
FIN-004.methodology: Benchmarks derived independently by bisection and simulation.

FIN-007.purpose: Show the full amortisation of a loan: the monthly payment, the split between interest and capital, and how the balance falls.
assumptions: A fixed rate for the whole term.
Payments made on schedule with no overpayments.
FIN-007.formula: Standard annuity payment, then a month-by-month schedule where each period's interest is `balance x monthly rate` and the remainder of the payment reduces the balance.
FIN-007.boundary: An illustration of contractual amortisation. Real lenders may apply daily interest, rounding, and fees that shift figures by small amounts.
FIN-007.methodology: First-year interest and capital were derived independently by explicit simulation.

FIN-008.purpose: Express monthly debt commitments as a proportion of gross monthly income.
FIN-008.scope: A ratio only. It does not assess affordability or model tax, essential spending or credit history.
assumptions: Income is gross (before tax).
Debt payments are the contractual monthly amounts.
FIN-008.formula: `DTI = total monthly debt / gross monthly income`. The front-end ratio is `housing payment / gross monthly income`.
validation: Zero income is rejected, because a ratio against zero income has no meaning.
FIN-008.boundary: Not a lending decision. Lenders use their own affordability rules and may assess net income, stress-tested rates and committed expenditure differently. The Low/Manageable/High bands are presentational guidance only.

FIN-010.purpose: Show how long a credit card takes to clear at a fixed monthly payment, and what payment clears it within a target time.
FIN-010.scope: A single card with a fixed payment and constant APR.
assumptions: No further spending on the card.
A constant APR.
Interest charged monthly on the outstanding balance.
FIN-010.formula: Payoff by month-by-month simulation. The payment needed for a target term uses the annuity formula `(B x r) / (1 - (1+r)^-n)`.
validation: A payment that never clears the balance is reported as a validation error rather than an infinite term.
FIN-010.boundary: An estimate. Real card interest depends on the issuer's daily calculation, statement dates, promotional rates and how payments are allocated between balance types.
FIN-010.methodology: Payoff months cross-checked against the closed form `n = -ln(1 - Br/P)/ln(1+r)`; the oracle reports any disagreement with its own simulation.

FIN-012.purpose: Compare keeping several debts against consolidating them into one loan.
FIN-012.scope: Existing revolving or fixed-payment debts against a single fixed-rate consolidation loan.
assumptions: Existing debts are repaid at their current monthly payments with no further borrowing.
The consolidation loan is fixed rate and fully amortising.
FIN-012.formula: Each existing debt is run to payoff by simulation to obtain its total interest. The consolidation loan uses the annuity formula on the combined balance plus any fee.
validation: An existing debt whose payment never clears its balance is reported explicitly, naming the debt.
FIN-012.boundary: Not a credit decision. The comparison deliberately reports the total interest change as well as the monthly payment change, because a longer consolidation term routinely lowers the monthly payment while increasing the total cost.
FIN-012.methodology: Both sides derived independently by simulation and bisection.

FIN-014.purpose: Work out an emergency fund target and how long it takes to reach it.
FIN-014.scope: Cash emergency savings against essential monthly spending.
assumptions: Essential spending is the unavoidable monthly total.
The fund is held in accessible cash, so no investment growth is assumed.
FIN-014.formula: `target = monthly essentials x months of cover`; `shortfall = max(0, target - current savings)`; months to target is `ceil(shortfall / monthly contribution)`.
validation: Zero essential spending is rejected. A zero contribution reports no completion date rather than an infinite one.
FIN-014.boundary: A planning aid, not financial advice. How many months of cover is appropriate depends on personal circumstances.

FIN-015.purpose: Work out the monthly saving needed to reach a target by a chosen date.
FIN-015.scope: Regular monthly saving into an interest-bearing account, with an optional starting balance.
assumptions: Contributions are made at the END of each month, so a contribution never earns interest before it is paid in.
A constant interest rate.
Interest compounds monthly.
FIN-015.formula: The existing balance grows to `S(1+r)^n`. The remainder is met by an ordinary annuity: `PMT = (target - S(1+r)^n) x r / ((1+r)^n - 1)`. Where the starting balance already exceeds the target, the required saving is zero.
FIN-015.boundary: An illustration. Interest rates change, and returns on anything other than cash are not guaranteed.
FIN-015.methodology: The required contribution was derived independently by bisection on a simulated month-by-month balance rather than by the annuity formula the engine uses.

PRO-005.purpose: Show how regular overpayments shorten a mortgage and cut total interest.
PRO-005.scope: Repayment mortgages with a level monthly overpayment.
assumptions: A fixed rate for the remaining term.
Overpayments are made every month and reduce capital immediately.
PRO-005.formula: Two amortisation simulations - baseline and with the overpayment - differenced for months and interest saved.
PRO-005.boundary: Not a quote. Many lenders cap annual overpayments (commonly 10% of the balance); check your mortgage terms.
PRO-005.methodology: Both scenarios simulated independently month by month in the oracle.

PRO-006.purpose: Compare staying on a current mortgage against remortgaging to a new deal.
PRO-006.scope: Fixed-rate comparison including product and legal fees.
assumptions: Both rates fixed for the periods compared.
Fees are added to the new loan.
PRO-006.formula: Annuity payment on each side; break-even is fees divided by the monthly saving.
PRO-006.boundary: Not a quote or a recommendation. Early repayment charges on the existing deal are NOT modelled and can be substantial.
PRO-006.methodology: Payments derived by bisection in the oracle.

PRO-007.purpose: Show interest-only payments against the capital-and-interest equivalent.
assumptions: A fixed rate.
No capital is repaid during the term.
PRO-007.formula: Monthly interest is balance x rate / 12. The repayment equivalent uses the annuity formula.
PRO-007.boundary: The full capital is still owed at the end of the term. A credible repayment plan is required; this calculator does not assess one.

PRO-009.purpose: Show what a mortgage payment becomes if interest rates rise.
PRO-009.scope: A single rate shock applied to the remaining term.
assumptions: The term and balance are unchanged.
The stressed rate applies for the whole remaining term.
PRO-009.formula: Annuity payment recomputed at the current rate plus the shock.
PRO-009.boundary: Lenders run their own stress tests with their own assumptions. This is not an affordability assessment.
PRO-009.methodology: Both payments derived by bisection in the oracle.

PRO-012.purpose: Work out equity in a property and how much could be released within a maximum LTV.
PRO-012.scope: A single property with one mortgage.
assumptions: The property value entered is accurate.
PRO-012.formula: Equity is value less balance; LTV is balance divided by value; available borrowing is value x max LTV less the balance, floored at zero.
PRO-012.boundary: Lenders use their own valuation and their own maximum LTV. Negative equity is reported honestly rather than floored.

PRO-014.purpose: Work out affordable rent, the income a landlord will require, and the upfront cost.
assumptions: Agents commonly require annual income of about 30x the monthly rent; the multiple is editable.
Deposit expressed in weeks of rent.
PRO-014.formula: Affordable rent is annual income divided by the multiple. Deposit is weekly rent (annual rent / 52) times the number of weeks.
PRO-014.boundary: Agency criteria differ. In England the tenancy deposit is capped at five weeks' rent where annual rent is under 50,000; this calculator does not enforce local caps.

PRO-015.purpose: Compare the long-run financial position of renting against buying.
PRO-015.scope: A holding period comparison including purchase tax, mortgage interest, maintenance, rent inflation and the opportunity cost of the deposit.
assumptions: Constant growth, rent inflation and investment return.
The deposit and purchase tax stay invested if renting.
PRO-015.formula: Both sides are reduced to a NET POSITION: buying is end equity less all cash paid in; renting is the grown investment pot less contributions less rent paid.
PRO-015.boundary: Extremely sensitive to assumptions that cannot be predicted. Not advice. Purchase tax uses the versioned rules for the selected jurisdiction.
PRO-015.methodology: Both sides re-implemented independently in the oracle, including the SDLT band table.
PRO-015.rules: Purchase tax from the versioned ruleset for the selected jurisdiction (SDLT, LBTT or LTT).

PRO-017.purpose: Appraise a rental property including purchase costs, yields and cash-on-cash return.
PRO-017.scope: Single buy-to-let purchase with an interest-only or repayment mortgage.
assumptions: Vacancy expressed as a percentage of gross rent.
Purchase tax at additional-property rates.
PRO-017.formula: Effective rent is gross rent net of vacancy; NOI deducts running costs; cash-on-cash divides pre-tax cash flow by cash invested.
PRO-017.boundary: Cash flow BEFORE income tax. Landlord income tax, mortgage interest relief restrictions and company structures are out of scope.
PRO-017.methodology: Independently recomputed in the oracle with a re-typed SDLT table.
PRO-017.rules: Purchase tax from the versioned ruleset for the selected jurisdiction.

PRO-020.purpose: Compare a geared property investment against an ungeared stock portfolio.
PRO-020.scope: Like-for-like on cash committed over a holding period.
assumptions: The same upfront cash and the same net periodic outlay go into the portfolio.
Constant growth and return rates.
PRO-020.formula: Property net gain is end equity less total cash invested. The portfolio starts with the same upfront cash and receives the property's net monthly outlay, compounded monthly.
PRO-020.boundary: Taxes on rental income and on investment gains are NOT modelled, and neither return is guaranteed. Not investment advice.
PRO-020.methodology: Both sides re-implemented independently in the oracle.
PRO-020.rules: Purchase tax from the versioned ruleset.

PRO-021.purpose: Show a rental property's annual and monthly cash flow before tax.
PRO-021.scope: Rent, vacancy, running costs and mortgage payments.
assumptions: Vacancy as a percentage of gross rent.
PRO-021.formula: Effective rent less costs less mortgage; cash-on-cash divides by cash invested.

PRO-022.purpose: Project property capital growth, in nominal and real terms.
PRO-022.scope: Compound growth at a constant rate.
assumptions: Constant growth and inflation.
PRO-022.formula: Final value is initial x (1+g)^n; the real value divides by (1+i)^n.
PRO-022.boundary: House prices do not grow smoothly and can fall. A projection, not a forecast.

PRO-024.purpose: Work out Stamp Duty Land Tax for a first-time buyer in England or Northern Ireland.
PRO-024.scope: First-time buyer relief on a single main residence.
assumptions: The buyer qualifies for first-time buyer relief.
PRO-024.formula: Relief bands applied where the price is within the qualifying ceiling; standard bands otherwise.
PRO-024.rules: SDLT bands, first-time buyer relief bands and the qualifying ceiling from the versioned ruleset, verified against gov.uk.
PRO-024.boundary: SDLT applies to England and Northern Ireland ONLY. Scotland charges LBTT and Wales charges LTT. Relief is lost entirely above the qualifying ceiling.
PRO-024.methodology: Band tables re-typed from gov.uk into the oracle and applied independently.
related: PRO-023 Stamp Duty Land Tax Calculator

PRO-025.purpose: Work out Stamp Duty Land Tax at the higher rates for an additional property in England or Northern Ireland.
PRO-025.scope: Additional dwellings, including buy-to-let and second homes.
assumptions: The higher-rate surcharge applies to the whole price.
PRO-025.formula: Standard bands plus a surcharge on the whole consideration.
PRO-025.rules: SDLT standard bands and the additional-property surcharge rate from the versioned ruleset.
PRO-025.boundary: England and Northern Ireland only. Does not model the refund available if a previous main residence is sold within the statutory period.
PRO-025.methodology: Band table and surcharge re-typed from gov.uk into the oracle.
related: PRO-023 Stamp Duty Land Tax Calculator
PRO-024 First-Time Buyer Stamp Duty Calculator

PRO-026.purpose: Work out Land and Buildings Transaction Tax on property in Scotland.
PRO-026.scope: Residential LBTT including first-time buyer relief and the Additional Dwelling Supplement.
assumptions: Residential rates only.
PRO-026.formula: Progressive LBTT bands. First-time buyer relief raises the nil-rate band; ADS is charged on the whole price where consideration reaches the statutory minimum.
PRO-026.rules: LBTT bands, first-time buyer nil-rate ceiling, ADS rate and ADS minimum consideration from the versioned ruleset, verified against revenue.scot.
PRO-026.boundary: LBTT applies to Scotland ONLY. England and Northern Ireland charge SDLT; Wales charges LTT.
PRO-026.methodology: LBTT bands and ADS re-typed from revenue.scot into the oracle, including the raised nil-rate band for first-time buyers.
related: PRO-023 Stamp Duty Land Tax Calculator

PRO-027.purpose: Work out Land Transaction Tax on property in Wales.
PRO-027.scope: Residential LTT at main and higher residential rates.
assumptions: Residential rates only.
PRO-027.formula: Progressive LTT bands. Additional properties use a SEPARATE higher-rate band table, not a surcharge added to the main rates.
PRO-027.rules: LTT main and higher residential bands from the versioned ruleset, verified against gov.wales. The higher rates in force are those effective from 11 December 2024.
PRO-027.boundary: LTT applies to Wales ONLY. Wales has NO first-time buyer relief; the main residential nil-rate band of 225,000 already applies to all main-residence purchases.
PRO-027.methodology: Both band tables re-typed from gov.wales into the oracle. A general rates page still showed pre-December-2024 higher rates; the ruleset was verified against the Welsh Government announcement rather than changed to match the stale page.
related: PRO-023 Stamp Duty Land Tax Calculator
